status.note: Built against ADR 0006. Only meaningful inside a Tabs; it has no standalone life and is not intended to grow one.

intent.purpose: One tab in a tab list: a label that selects a panel when chosen. It carries its own identity and its own disabled state, and nothing else — whether it is selected is a comparison, not a property it holds.
behaviour: Compares its `value` against the selection on the surrounding Tabs to decide whether it is selected. It cannot be told directly.
Selects itself on click, unless a caller's own onClick called preventDefault first.
Shows an indicator along its bottom edge when selected. It is rendered only while selected and is out of flow, so selecting never changes the row's height.
Shows a wash behind its label on hover, drawn as its own layer so the label does not fade with it.
Renders a heavier label while pressed, and the resting weight otherwise.
Throws if rendered outside a Tabs. There is no selection to compare against, and looking unselected would hide the mistake.
notFor: Use outside a Tabs. It has no fallback behaviour and deliberately fails loudly instead.
Carrying an icon or a count badge. Neither is designed; adding one would be inventing a component nobody has reviewed.
Acting as a link. It renders a button and changes no URL — a tab that navigates is a nav item.
Holding the panel's content. That is TabPanel's job, and keeping them apart is what lets the panels live outside the tablist.

selected.description: Derived from the surrounding Tabs by comparing `value`. Not settable on this component. Reaches the DOM as both `aria-selected` and a `data-ds-state` on the indicator.
selected.visual: An indicator bar appears along the bottom edge.

disabled.description: Set by the `disabled` prop, and rendered as a natively disabled button.
disabled.visual: The label takes the disabled text colour and the pointer cursor is dropped.

hover.description: The pointer is over the item and it is not disabled.
hover.visual: A rounded wash appears behind the label.

focus-visible.description: Focused in a way the browser judges worth showing a ring for — keyboard, not a mouse click.
focus-visible.visual: A dashed ring is drawn inside the item's box. The indicator is unaffected, so a focused selected tab still reads as selected.

active.description: A pointer or key is held down on the item — the CSS `:active` state. Note the collision of vocabulary: the design source labels its SELECTED specimen 'Active'. This is not that; this is the press.
active.visual: The label switches to the medium weight. That is wider than the resting weight, so the row shifts for the duration of the press — a known and accepted cost, recorded in ADR 0006.

a11y.keyboard: Reachable with Tab only when selected; the arrow keys on the parent move focus here and select in one action. Space and Enter activate, as they do on any button.
notes: `disabled` renders a native disabled button, so the tab is removed from the focus order and cannot be reached at all. A keyboard user therefore cannot land on it to discover it exists. The alternative, `aria-disabled`, keeps it discoverable but leaves it clickable unless every handler guards; the native form was chosen because the authoring contract says to use the pseudo-class the browser owns.
The accessible name is whatever is passed as children. An item given a non-text child — an icon alone, say — has no name and nothing here detects that.

`aria-controls` always points at the id its matching TabPanel would use, whether or not that panel is rendered. A tab with no panel therefore references a missing id, which some assistive technology reports. Rendering a panel per item is the caller's obligation.

Contrast is claimed as AA for the resting label against the app's surface: `text/primary` is white on the dark ground the design source uses. It is NOT claimed for the disabled label, which is intentionally low contrast, nor for any other background a consumer places this on.
The whole item is the hit target, not just the label, so the target is the full 52px row height.

children.description: The label. Text only in every designed example; nothing enforces that.

root.description: The button. Owns the focus ring, the pressed weight and the disabled colour, and stretches to share the row equally with its siblings.

label.description: The text, and the box the hover wash is drawn behind. Truncates with an ellipsis rather than widening the row.

indicator.description: The bar along the bottom edge that marks the selected tab. Present only while selected — it is out of flow, so its arrival and departure move nothing. Pulled down over the list's track so the two share an edge rather than stacking.
